original.target_description: Unresolved target: supplied study_o is Study 1, whereas locator p. 9–11 (PDF pages 9–11; printed pp. 173–175) covers Study 2 results and the start of Study 3. Study 1 reports separate scenario-level binomial tests without a uniquely identified scenario.

n.sample_role: Unresolved analytic unit/test. Candidate Study 1 counts: 176 total participants; Airplane 24 participants; Mall 20 participants; 226 responses across eight scenarios. These are distinct roles, not mutually exclusive final groups to sum.
n.exclusions: Scenario-specific binomial-test denominator and handling of neutral preferences not explicitly established for a uniquely identified target. No N inferred from degrees of freedom.
n.location: Study 1 Method and Results, printed p. 169 / PDF p. 5; contrast Study 2 Results, printed pp. 173–174 / PDF pp. 9–10.
n.quote: All the subjects (176 in total) were undergraduate students at the University ... The numbers of subjects varied from 20 to 40 for different scenarios. The ... Airplane scenario (below) had 24, and the Mall had 20. ... Each scenario showed a ... significant preference for indirect harm by a binomial test ( p < 0.001).

notes: Only n_o assigned; replication, effect-size, p, and reported-success fields are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguous: Study 1 has eight separate scenario tests, and the neutral description does not identify which one. Printed total 176 participants is not adopted as a critical-test analytic N; 226 is explicitly responses, not participants. Airplane 24 and Mall 20 are candidate scenario sample sizes only, not a documented sum. Study 2 on locator pages gives the unadjusted morality test t53 = 5.12, p = 0.0000, one-tailed, and across eight cases t7 = 3.47, p = 0.0052, one-tailed; Table I is explicitly based on 8 × 54 observations. The adjusted analysis restricts to directness-agreement cases (49.3%) and recodes responses involving intention/appearance/probability (71% of total assigned equally immoral), then reports t50 = 3.24, p = .0011, one tailed, and scenario t7 = 6.26, p = .0002. These remain candidate tests from a different study; no analytic participant N is derived from their df. No candidate selected by numeric matching or row order. PDF pages 5, 6, 9, 10, 11 visually inspected; canonical text supplies evidence.
